summary: This Game Theory lecture extends the prediction-method, power-alchemy, and strategy lenses by treating a possible U.S.-China grand bargain as a testable payoff engine: public hostility is theater only if it predicts a concrete exchange across finance, energy, AI chips, Taiwan routing, and Treasury demand.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The class calls the visible U.S.-China friction theater, then attaches a prediction discipline: the model should become testable within days.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public read already links this source to the Prediction child page because the active mechanism is not generic cynicism about theater; it is theater constrained by named players, payoffs, and a near-term falsification window.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Stablecoins turn the Treasury problem into household and platform demand, with financial repression available if voluntary uptake is not enough.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The Power As Alchemy page already uses this source because the stablecoin passage shows sovereign debt becoming ordinary money use, legal compliance, and platform-mediated demand.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep this source as the May 14 practical case where a theater claim is disciplined by prediction: visible friction only counts as game-theory evidence if Jiang names the larger bargain, the payoff exchange, and the short horizon on which the model can fail.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Prediction owns the falsification discipline. Game Theory owns the player/payoff map; Stories owns theater only when the public narrative itself captures imagination.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the lecture as the operational diagram behind the stablecoin debt-transfer anchor: U.S. debt-service pressure seeks Treasury buyers, stablecoins can route retail demand into Treasury backing, and legal requirements can turn a fiscal burden into compulsory monetary reality.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Power As Alchemy owns debt becoming lived money and compulsion. Mass Society owns transaction surveillance if population administration becomes primary; Strategy owns Taiwan, energy, and chokepoints when material access is the active test.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold this source for a future bargain-sequencing pass: Jiang reads the Trump-Xi visit through players, constraints, and mutually desired payoffs, then reduces morality and sovereignty objections to what each actor can get inside the deal.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns the payoff audit and player map. Prediction owns whether the forecast risks being wrong; Power As Alchemy owns the monetary conversion; Strategy owns the energy and Taiwan material board.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the lecture only as supporting evidence for the access-control bargain: China wants cheap energy and market access, while Taiwan can be reframed as a pressure-transfer problem involving South Korea and Japan.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: The Strategy child page should not absorb the whole grand-bargain model. It owns trade routes, energy access, Taiwan geography, and regional pressure transfer only when those material constraints are the active mechanism.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-05-14 lecture is the dated public classroom formulation of the Trump-Xi grand-bargain forecast before the late-May Holy Empire and predictive-history synthesis sources.

The source explicitly ties the 2026 bargain model back to Jiang's reading of the 1972 Nixon opening, the post-gold dollar problem, petrodollar demand, manufacturing, and strategic ambiguity around Taiwan.

Within the current public lens chronology, this source sits after the January 2026 grand-bargain forecast and before the May 21 reserve-privilege/addiction lecture, making it the bridge where bargain sequencing, stablecoin debt transfer, and Taiwan pressure routing become one classroom model.

next_actions.action: Do not create a new public grand-bargain concept from this source alone; the Prediction child page already has a bargain-as-sequence anchor, and Power As Alchemy already carries the debt-transfer mechanism.

When next touching Game Theory, compare this source with the January 5 grand-bargain forecast and the May 28 final examination to decide whether bargain sequencing belongs as a Game Theory subsection or remains inside Prediction.
If adding more Taiwan material, keep the boundary narrow: use this source for pressure transfer to South Korea and Japan, not for generic Taiwan-sovereignty prose.
